title: Vault
openFor: Unlocked · {minutes, plural, =0 {locks shortly} one {locks in # min} other {locks in # min}}
clipboardClears: · Cleared from the clipboard in {seconds} s
copyFailed: Could not copy: the browser does not allow clipboard access.
pickItem: Select an item to see its details
notFound: This vault does not exist or you have no access.
noPersonal: You have no personal vault in this organization yet.
totpInvalid: The TOTP key could not be read.

roleHint.read: Opens and copies items, gets TOTP codes.
roleHint.edit: Also adds, changes and trashes items.
roleHint.manage: Also grants and removes access; sees the log.

guest.title: The vault is not available to guests
guest.body: Guest accounts have no personal vault; ask an organization member for anything that must be shared.

error.load: The vault could not be loaded.
error.decrypt: Decryption failed: wrong key or password.
error.recoveryTypo: The recovery key has a typo; check the characters.
error.weakKdf: The key derivation settings from the server are not safe; stopped.

setup.title: Create your vault password
setup.body: The vault opens with a password separate from your account password. It never leaves your device: we cannot see it, and we cannot reset it if you forget it.
setup.rulePersonal: Does not contain your email or name
setup.ruleLeaked: Not in leaked password lists (checked on the device)
setup.tip: Pick a long, memorable passphrase, e.g. four random words. Do not reuse your account password.

how.title: How does zero knowledge work?
how.cost: Even a compromised server cannot read the vault. The price: if you lose both your password and your recovery key, nobody can reach your vault's data.
how.passkeyLater: A passkey can be added after setup

recovery.title: Keep your recovery key
recovery.body: If you forget your vault password, only this key opens your vault. It is shown only now; we do not keep it.
recovery.notInVault: Do not store this key inside the vault. You cannot reach it while the vault is locked.
recovery.saved: I saved my recovery key somewhere safe
recovery.fileHint: Print this file and keep it safe, then delete it from your computer.

keep.title: Where to keep it?
keep.printTitle: Print it, keep it in a drawer, not the vault
keep.printBody: Paper survives server and device loss.
keep.usbTitle: Download it to an encrypted USB drive
keep.usbBody: Encrypt it separately if it goes to a cloud folder.
keep.envelopeTitle: A sealed envelope with someone you trust
keep.envelopeBody: For team vaults a second manager is a better way.
keep.admins: Admins cannot open your personal vault either. Items in space vaults stay reachable by that vault's other managers.

unlock.title: Vault locked
unlock.wrong: Wrong vault password. {remaining, plural, one {# try left} other {# tries left}}, then you need to wait 30 s.
unlock.wait: Too many wrong attempts. Try again in {seconds} s.

reason.manual: Locked at {time} · you stay signed in
reason.idle: Locked at {time} after inactivity · you stay signed in
reason.hidden: Locked at {time} when the tab was hidden · you stay signed in
reason.system: Locked at {time} when the computer locked · your account stays signed in

recoverFlow.title: Open with the recovery key
recoverFlow.body: Type the recovery key you saved during setup. Spaces and dashes do not matter.
recoverFlow.newPassword: Your vault is open. Now set a new vault password; the old one stops working.

passkey.unsupported: This browser or key does not support unlocking with a passkey (WebAuthn PRF).
passkey.notOnDevice: No passkey for this vault was found on this device, or the prompt was cancelled. Add one for this device in Vault › Settings.
passkey.addBody: Open the vault in a second with Touch ID, Windows Hello or a security key. The key derived from the passkey never leaves this device.
passkey.label: Name

detail.subtitle: {vault} vault · {type}
detail.expired: This item has expired. Renew it and save the new value here.
detail.expiresIn: {days, plural, =0 {Expires today.} one {Expires in # day.} other {Expires in # days.}} Renew it and save the new value here.
detail.noteHint: The content is in the notes below.
detail.tampered: This item could not be opened
detail.rollback: An older version of this item was served
detail.tamperedBody: The encrypted content failed verification; it may have been altered or swapped with another item. Tell the vault manager.

history.title: Version history
history.body: The last 10 versions are kept. Going back to one saves it as a new version.
history.empty: This item has no earlier version.
history.hint: Versions are decrypted on this device; the server cannot see their content.

trash.purgeConfirm: Delete "{name}" forever? This cannot be undone.
trash.banner: Will be deleted forever on {date} · {days} days left. Deleted by {who}.
trash.emptyConfirm: Delete every item in the trash forever?
trash.hint: Items in the trash do not show in search or quick access cards.

form.name: Name
form.tagsHint: Press Enter or comma to add
form.totpHint: Paste an otpauth:// link or the secret key
form.encryptedUpload: Encrypted on the device before upload · up to 100 MB
form.saveBeforeAttach: Save the item first to add attachments.

empty.title: Your vault is ready and empty
empty.body: Add your first item or bring your Vaultwarden data with a Bitwarden JSON file. Everything is encrypted on this device.
empty.passkeyBody: Open the vault in a second with Touch ID or a security key.
empty.spaceBody: A shared vault for team passwords. Use + in the sidebar; access is granted person by person.

newVault.title: Create a space vault
newVault.body: The vault key is made on this device and wrapped for you only. You grant members access one by one afterwards.
newVault.name: Vault name

access.title: Access
access.summary: {items, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} · {people, plural, one {# person has access} other {# people have access}} · created {date}
access.noKeys: Has not set up their vault
access.staleTitle: {count, plural, one {# person} other {# people}} left the space but still hold the vault key
access.staleBody: {names}. Removing their access and rotating the key is recommended.
access.rotationNote: Removing access rotates the vault key: {count, plural, one {# item is} other {# items are}} re-encrypted on your device with a new key, wrapped again for the remaining members. Old copies on the removed person's device cannot open new items.
access.settingsRolledBack: Your vault settings on the server are older than the ones this device last saw. An old app version can cause this, and so can a server handing back an old copy. Keys cannot be verified for now, so you are asked before a key is sealed to anyone.
access.settingsUnreadable: Your vault settings on the server would not open. Keys cannot be verified for now, so you are asked before a key is sealed to anyone, and your settings are not saved beyond this session.
access.selfRemoveNote: You cannot remove your own access: your device would make the new key, so rotating would not protect the vault from you. Ask another person with "Manage" access to do it.
access.twoManagers: At least two people with "Manage" are recommended; if a single manager loses both vault password and recovery key, the vault cannot be recovered.
access.grantBody: The {vault} vault key is wrapped on this device with the chosen person's public key; only the wrapped copy goes to the server.
access.notSetUp: Has not set up their vault
access.willJoinSpace: {name} is not a member of {space}; granting access also adds them to the space as Viewer.
access.step2: The {vault} vault key is wrapped with it on this device.
access.step3: Only the wrapped key goes to the server.
access.compareHint: To be sure, compare the fingerprint with the one on {name}'s Vault › Settings screen.

tofu.unverified: The key records in your vault settings may be incomplete, so this key cannot be verified
tofu.unverifiedConfirm: The key of {name} cannot be verified, because the key records in your vault settings may be incomplete. If you are not sure, compare the fingerprint with them. I trust this key anyway.
tofu.changed: This person's key differs from the one seen before
tofu.invalid: The fingerprint reported by the server does not match the key; access cannot be granted.
tofu.changedConfirm: {name}'s public key differs from the one you saw before. They may have set up their vault again; if unsure, compare the fingerprint with them. I trust this key anyway.

rotate.blockedTitle: The rotation stopped at these items
rotate.blockedBody: These do not open with the current key, so they cannot move to the new one. Nothing has changed. They have to be cleared before anyone can be removed from this vault.
rotate.blockedCurrent: the current version does not open; the item has to be deleted from the vault for good
rotate.unnamedItem: Item whose name cannot be read
rotate.deleteRevisionBody: This cannot be undone. This old version is deleted for all members; the current item and its other versions stay. It is written to the access log.
rotate.confirmKeysTitle: The new key would also be sealed to these people; check them first
rotate.confirmKeys: I checked the fingerprints and trust these keys.

why.first_seen: nobody has confirmed this key yet
why.changed: their key differs from the one you saw before
why.unlisted: you did not see this key on the list

rotate.title: Remove access for {names}
rotate.body: A new vault key is generated, {count, plural, one {# item is} other {# items are}} re-encrypted on this device and the key is wrapped for the remaining members.
rotate.doneBody: {names} can no longer open new items in this vault.
rotate.suggest: Consider changing {count, plural, one {# password} other {# passwords}} they may have seen:

log.title: Access log
log.retention: Entries are append-only, cannot be deleted and are kept for 1 year.

import.body: Choose the file you exported in Vaultwarden or Bitwarden under Tools › Export vault. It is read in this browser and never sent to the server.
import.formats: Bitwarden JSON, password-protected JSON, Bitwarden CSV or a Chrome password export (CSV)
import.localOnly: read on this device, not sent to the server
import.found: {folders} folders, {collections} organization collections · TOTP in {totp} items · custom fields in {fields} items
import.plainWarning: This file is not encrypted. Delete it from your computer and Downloads folder when the import is done.
import.mapTitle: Which item goes to which vault?
import.tagFolders: Add the folder name as a tag
import.convertApi: Turn {count} notes named token, API key or PAT into API keys
import.skipDupes: Skip items already in the vault (same name, username and site) · {count} matches
import.failedRows: {count, plural, one {# row in the file could not be read and will not be imported} other {# rows in the file could not be read and will not be imported}}. Other items are not affected.
import.run: {count, plural, one {Encrypt and import # item} other {Encrypt and import # items}}
import.done: {count, plural, one {# item imported} other {# items imported}}
import.doneBody: Encrypted on your device and uploaded · {seconds} s
import.deleteFile: Delete the export file now. Before shutting down Vaultwarden, follow the team's move in Vault health.

kind.account_encrypted: Account-restricted encrypted exports cannot be read. Export again in Bitwarden with the "password protected" option.

error.invalid_file: The file could not be read; make sure it is a Bitwarden export.
error.password_required: This file needs its export password.
error.account_encrypted: Account-restricted encrypted exports cannot be read; export again as password protected.
error.unsupported: This file's encryption settings are not supported.

warning.attachments_missing: Attachment not in the export; upload it by hand
warning.passkey_not_migrated: Saved passkey could not be moved
warning.linked_field_dropped: Linked field could not be moved
warning.multiple_collections: Was in several collections; added to the first

health.title: Vault health
health.checked: {ok} of the {total} items you can access are fine.
health.scope: The report covers only the items you can access; the server cannot see passwords, so there is no organization-wide report.
health.breachOff: The leaked password check is turned off in your organization; the report only covers checks done on your device.
health.breachFailed: The leak check service could not be reached; some passwords were not checked. Scan again later.

settings.title: Settings
settings.heading: Vault settings
settings.body: Lock, clipboard, unlock methods and recovery. Settings belong to your account and are stored encrypted.
settings.hiddenHint: This long after you switch to another tab or app. Come back sooner and it stays open.
settings.close: Lock when the tab or browser closes
settings.closeHint: The key is kept in memory only
settings.clipboardClear: Clear copied values from the clipboard
settings.clipboardHint: If the clipboard still holds what we copied
settings.passkeysHint: Touch ID, Windows Hello or a security key (WebAuthn PRF)
settings.newRecoveryBody: Creating a new recovery key invalidates the old one at once.
settings.exportBody: The {count} items you can access are written to a Bitwarden-compatible file encrypted with this password. Keep the file safe.
settings.changePasswordBody: Your private key is re-wrapped with the new password on this device; the vault content does not change.
settings.hiddenDesktopHint: This wait starts when you switch to another tab or app. In the desktop app minimising and the tray do not count; the vault locks at once when Windows locks or the computer sleeps.

share.title: One-time link
share.body: Send this item to someone outside your organization. The link is limited in time and number of opens and is deleted after the last one.
share.disabled: Your organization has turned off vault share links.
share.includeTotp: Also send the verification code (TOTP) key (the recipient could generate codes indefinitely)
share.zeroKnowledge: The item is encrypted on this device with a new key. The key is only after the # in the link and never reaches the server. Password history and attachments are not sent.
share.onceHint: You can only see this link now. It can be opened at most {views} times within {hours}.
share.none: This item has no open links.

publicShare.title: A vault item was sent to you
publicShare.limits: This link can be opened {views, plural, one {# more time} other {# more times}} and is valid until {date}.
publicShare.zeroKnowledge: The content is decrypted in this browser; the key is inside the link and is not sent to the server. Showing it uses one open.
publicShare.viewsLeft: This link can be opened {count, plural, one {# more time} other {# more times}}. Nothing stays on this device once you close the page.
publicShare.lastView: This was the last open; the link no longer works. Save what you need now.
publicShare.noKeyBody: Make sure you copied the whole link (including everything after #), or ask the sender for a new one.
publicShare.badKey: The link could not be opened
publicShare.gone: The link has expired or has been used
publicShare.disabled: This link can no longer be used
publicShare.goneBody: Ask the sender for a new link.

policy.title: Organization policy
policy.body: These settings apply to everyone's vault in the organization; only admins see them.
policy.breachHint: Only the first 5 characters of a password's SHA-1 hash are sent (k-anonymity); the password and the full hash never leave the device.
policy.mirrorHint: If your server has no internet access, the address of a Have I Been Pwned mirror or proxy. Leave empty to use the public service.
policy.shareLinksHint: When off, no new links can be created and open links stop working.

hello.offerBody: Open the vault with {name} instead of typing your master password. The key stays encrypted on this computer, protected by the operating system; your master password is asked again every {days} days and after it changes.
hello.expired: It has been {days} days since you last used your master password. Open with it once, then {name} works again.
hello.gone: {name} can no longer be used on this computer. Open with your master password; you can set it up again in Settings.
hello.failed: Could not open with {name}. You can open with your master password.
hello.settingsHint: On this computer only. Your master password is asked every {days} days and after it changes.

searchAll.more: {count, plural, one {# more item} other {# more items}}

move.title: Move to another vault
move.titleMany: {count, plural, one {Move # item to another vault} other {Move # items to another vault}}
move.body: {name} is re-encrypted on this device with the chosen vault's key.
move.bodyMany: The items are re-encrypted on this device with the chosen vault's key.
move.noTarget: There is no other vault you can write to.
move.doneMany: {count, plural, one {# item moved to {vault}} other {# items moved to {vault}}}
